edges.description: The enzyme's substrates have no alternative route out, so they accumulate. The founding metabolic study framed this as the expected consequence and then measured it.
The accumulated oxysterols are themselves toxic to the relevant human neurons at the concentrations found in patients, which is the step that converts a biochemical abnormality into a mechanism.
Why a diffuse metabolic insult produces a length-dependent degeneration of the corticospinal tract, rather than a generalised cortical disease, is not established in any located source.
Gait ataxia is common in SPG5 and is not straightforwardly explained by corticospinal degeneration alone, which is part of why the "pure" classification of this disease has been questioned.
Loss of descending corticospinal control of the detrusor produces urgency, the usual bladder consequence of an upper motor neuron lesion.
The knockout accumulates the oxysterol but does not develop the neurological disease, so it does not reproduce the step this entry treats as pathogenic.
edges.limitations: The most likely reason is dose, not mechanism: plasma 27-hydroxycholesterol in the knockout is about a fifth of the patient level, and the human neuron experiment that establishes toxicity used patient-range concentrations. A model that never reaches the toxic concentration cannot test whether the concentration is toxic. The same source notes a cyp27a1 transgenic mouse with raised 27-hydroxycholesterol and likewise no neurological symptoms.

edges.description: Elevated serum and cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol is the direct measurement of the accumulating substrate.
Serum levels track disease severity and duration, so the marker carries information about how far the degeneration has gone and not only that the enzyme is absent.
A second stranded substrate of the same enzyme, confirming the block is at CYP7B1 rather than downstream.

nodes.description: Atorvastatin 40 mg/day for nine weeks lowered serum 27-hydroxycholesterol by 31.5% in a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in 14 SPG5 patients, against a primary endpoint of serum 27-hydroxycholesterol. Read the result carefully: the trial met a biomarker endpoint, not a clinical one; cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol fell only 8.4% and did not separate from placebo; and no clinical effect was seen or expected over nine weeks. It is described by its authors as the first causal treatment strategy in hereditary spastic paraplegia, which is a claim about the strategy rather than about demonstrated clinical benefit.

evidence.snippet: The SPG5A subtype of Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (HSP) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the CYP7B1 gene, which encodes a steroid cytochrome P450 7α-hydroxylase.

evidence.reference_title: CYP7B1: novel mutations and magnetic resonance spectroscopy abnormalities in hereditary spastic paraplegia type 5A.
evidence.snippet: Four novel mutations were identified; one frameshift (c.509 delT p.L170fs), one premature stop codon (c.334 C>T p.R112X), one amino acid changing (c.440 G>A p.G147D) and one duplication (c.945_947 dupGGC p.A316AA).

nodes.description: Biallelic CYP7B1 variants reduce or abolish oxysterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, a cytochrome P450 expressed in brain and liver. Reported alleles include nonsense changes (p.R63X, p.R112X, p.Y275X) and missense changes clustering at the C-terminal end of the protein in exon 6, with residue R417 recurring often enough to be described as a mutational hot spot.

evidence.reference_title: CYP7B1 mutations in pure and complex forms of hereditary spastic paraplegia type 5.
evidence.snippet: Three of these mutations were nonsense (p.R63X, p.R112X, p.Y275X) and five were missense mutations (p.T297A, p.R417H, p.R417C, p.F470I, p.R486C), the last four clustering in exon 6 at the C-terminal end of the protein. Residue R417 appeared as a mutational hot-spot.

nodes.description: Progressive degeneration of the corticospinal tract motor neurons is the defining lesion of hereditary spastic paraplegia as a class, and SPG5 is one instance of it. White matter hyperintensities on brain MRI accompany it in a substantial minority, including in families whose clinical phenotype is otherwise pure.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary spastic paraplegia type 5: natural history, biomarkers and a randomized controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: Spastic paraplegia type 5 (SPG5) is a rare subtype of hereditary spastic paraplegia, a highly heterogeneous group of neurodegenerative disorders defined by progressive neurodegeneration of the corticospinal tract motor neurons.

nodes.description: The Cyp7b1 knockout mouse raises circulating 27-hydroxycholesterol but has no neurological symptoms. That negative result is informative rather than a failed experiment: the absolute plasma 27-hydroxycholesterol in the knockout is only about 20% of the level measured in patients, so the model is consistent with a concentration threshold the mouse never reaches.

A common feature, and one that complicates the historical classification of SPG5 as a pure spastic paraplegia — a pure HSP should not have prominent cerebellar signs. An earlier study separately found a coding polymorphism in CYP7B1 significantly associated with cerebellar signs complicating an HSP phenotype.
FREQUENT is the band that the source's word "common" maps to; no percentage is given anywhere in the located literature.

nodes.description: Oxysterols at patient concentrations impair metabolic activity and viability of human cortical neurons. The experiment was done in human neurons and dosed to the levels measured in patients, which is the strongest link in this chain — but note it establishes that these concentrations are toxic to cortical neurons in culture, not that the same process selects the long corticospinal axons in vivo.

evidence.snippet: Oxysterols were found to impair metabolic activity and viability of human cortical neurons at concentrations found in SPG5 patients, indicating that elevated levels of oxysterols might be key pathogenic factors in SPG5.

nodes.description: 27-hydroxycholesterol and 25-hydroxycholesterol accumulate. The magnitudes differ by compartment and by species of oxysterol in a way that matters: plasma 27-hydroxycholesterol rises 6- to 9-fold, cerebrospinal fluid 27-hydroxycholesterol 30- to 50-fold, and plasma 25-hydroxycholesterol about 100-fold, while 25-hydroxycholesterol is not measurable in cerebrospinal fluid at all. Bile acid synthesis itself is normal, so this is a substrate-stranding lesion and not a bile acid deficiency.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate here that four patients with the SPG5 disease have 6- to 9-fold increased plasma levels of 27-hydroxycholesterol. A much higher increase, 30- to 50-fold, was found in cerebrospinal fluid.

nodes.description: A frameshift and an in-frame duplication, among four novel variants found in four unrelated SPG5A patients. They are recorded because they extend the allelic spectrum beyond the nonsense and missense classes above, which matters when the pathograph root is loss of function: frameshift, nonsense, missense and duplication alleles all converge on the same enzyme deficiency.
Missense changes at residue R417, described as a mutational hot spot; part of a cluster of missense variants at the C-terminal end of the protein in exon 6.
Nonsense variants reported in autosomal recessive HSP families.
